claims.explanation: Pyrimethamine is a DHFR inhibitor, and its selective anticancer activity likely reflects dependence on folate/one-carbon metabolism and nucleotide biosynthesis, with sensitivity determined by DHFR expression and by loss of alternative nucleotide salvage or DNA-repair pathways. The transcriptional similarity to methotrexate and raltitrexed supports an antifolate/thymidylate-synthesis mechanism, while resistance may arise from high expression of DHFR or SLC47A1-mediated efflux. TP53 and other mutations are common in both sensitive and resistant lines, so they are weak predictors; the strongest genomic features should relate to folate pathway dependence and drug transport.
